msgs: Water at a trail angel's water cache. Not on any map. Thank you, whoever keeps it running.
Found a trail angel's water cache the map doesn't show. Green and full of bugs. Filtered two litres anyway.
STATELINE. Utah! The sign, the register, a photo with my last bit of water. Walked all of Arizona.
Grand Canyon Village. Stood at the rim with a crowd of tourists and just stared. The trail goes all the way down to the river and all the way up the other side.
Took the Flagstaff Urban Route (Passage 33): 14 miles instead of 31 on the main line (17 fewer).
Day 1. Shuttle to Montezuma Pass, walked down to the border monument at the fence, touched it, and turned around to start north solo. Straight up into the Huachucas.
Done at Stateline. Waited for my ride on the dirt road with a cold drink from the cooler someone left. It's over.
Dry camp, and not enough water for dinner. Ate cold tortillas and went to bed thirsty.
Freeman Road cache season (NOBO). Hot food, cold drinks, camp chairs. Stayed way longer than planned.
A day hiker gave me an orange. Best orange of my life.
Older couple on a day hike gave me a peach and asked a million questions. Lovely.
Weekend backpackers gave away their extra food at the trailhead. Scored a whole sleeve of Oreos.
Somebody's abandoned Snickers in a ziplock on a trail sign, with a note: "for a thru-hiker". Me!
Section hiker heading the other way handed me a cold Gatorade from his pack. Who carries that?
Counted on a trail angel's water cache. Bone dry.
Pouring rain all day. Tent day. Read the same three pages of my book over and over.
